publicPrompt:
Play the available Mars Workshop campaign through the public interface, pursuing its goals in an order you choose. You may finish when the campaign is complete, or stop earlier if you no longer want to continue. You need not use a particular method, avoid simple solutions, or produce a long run.

Use only the public CLI and the setup metadata file. Do not read source code, tests, analyst documents, witnesses, solver output or other players' records. You may inspect all public rules, recipes, partners, object/place details and exact previews. Output filtering is allowed. Do not write programs that choose moves; manually selected actions may be executed in sequence.

Session: fun-workshop-v1-full-pilot-1.
Initialize from the repository root with:
node experiments/mars-workshop-play.ts init fun-workshop-v1-full-pilot-1 ordinary "$(cat results/mars-workshop-prompts/fun-workshop-v1-full-pilot-1.json)"
The metadata file is permitted setup data containing this assignment and your participant identifier.

The init output and inspect SESSION cli give the command guide. Available commands include view, inspect, catalogue, partners, preview, combine/act, select, undo, checkpoint, report, finish and verify. There is no required move count. Simple or unexpectedly short solutions remain valid.

Play normally rather than explaining every move. At the first newly completed goal, and once again after at least six distinct goals have been completed, record one brief checkpoint using exactly this question:
"What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?"
Record the question and answer verbatim. If a single action skips a boundary, ask once afterward, not repeatedly. If you stop before a boundary, omit that checkpoint.

At campaign completion or your chosen stopping point, answer this open question with report:
"How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?"
Record the question and answer verbatim, then finish and verify your capture.

Give an honest account rather than praise for the researcher. Familiar or obvious actions need not be criticized for being familiar. Equally, unwanted work should be reported. Your report describes this AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
condition: ordinary catalogue; full campaign assignment; public interface only
exposureHistory: No prior Workshop implementation, analyst documentation, witnesses or player records supplied before this assignment.
